parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Electrons, each of mass *m* and charge *q*, are accelerated from rest in a vacuum through a potential difference *V*.

Derive an expression, in terms of *m*, *q* and *V*, for the final speed *v* of the electrons. Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The accelerated electrons in (b) are injected at point S into a region of uniform magnetic field of flux density *B*, as illustrated in Fig. 8.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The electrons move at right angles to the direction of the magnetic field. The path of the electrons is a circle of radius *r*.
parts.text:
Show that the specific charge *q*/*m* of the electrons is given by the expression

*q*/*m* = 2*V*/(*B*²*r*²).

Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference *V* of 230 V. The electrons are injected normally into the magnetic field of flux density 0.38 mT. The radius *r* of the circular orbit of the electrons is 14 cm.

Use this information to calculate a value for the specific charge of an electron.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why the arrangement outlined in (ii), using the same values of *B* and *V*, is not practical for the determination of the specific charge of α-particles.

figures.caption: Fig. 8.1
figures.alt: A dashed circular electron path begins at point S inside a shaded region of uniform magnetic field, with callouts identifying the field and the path radius r.
